# dsh-workspace-browser
Standalone Cordis client plugin that gives the shipped dsh web client the workspace features it does
not have: the sidebar **Recents** section, collapsible section headers, the **project editor** with
extra source folders, pin/rename/fork/archive row actions, search, shortcuts, and the conversation-
hero **workspace picker**. In the project editor a folder's own name opens that folder in the OS fil
e manager, and a conversation whose own folder has vanished is silently re-rooted to the Workspace's
primary folder when it is opened.
## Why it exists
The 2026-09-29 Desktop build (**0.2.0-rc.2**) shipped a workspace browser with no Recents, no collap
sible sections and no project editor. By **0.2.1-rc.2** the in-tree `ui-workspace` is that browser (
toast factory, inline session-id copy, shared hover dwell, session watermarks, remote-access hooks)
but still has no Recents section, no project editor and no folder API. This plugin still replaces th
at row: the rc.2 contracts come from the in-tree snapshot, and the plugin layer on top is Recents, t
he project editor, and the plugin-owned source-folder list.
`cordis.patch.yml` disables the in-tree `ui-workspace` row and inserts this package as `ui-workspace
-browser`. A `name` override cannot do that swap: the include loader treats `name` as an identity ch
eck and skips the patch when it does not match, so the stock browser would keep running and this plu
gin's Recents, project editor, and source folders would never mount. Both claim the same slots, loca
le namespace (`workspace`) and `ctx.uiWorkspace` service, so only one may be enabled. While this bun
dle is selected, `ui-workspace-browser` must stay enabled — disabling only that row leaves nobody pr
oviding the service and web boot times out. A bundle whose slots never register therefore leaves the
workspace region **empty**, which is why the client-half surface is checked against the host before
any install (see Verification).
## Source folders on a host without the folder API
`addFolder` / `removeFolder` / `setPrimaryFolder` and the `folders` projection on a workspace view e
xist only on the newer workspace controller; the shipped host has none of them. The plugin owns the
newer workspace controller; the shipped host has none of them. The plugin owns the first two there:
- the folder list lives in the plugin's own persisted viewing store (`persist: 'dsh.workspace.view.v
5'`) and is also written to `.dsh/storages/workspace-browser-folders.json`. A copied `.dsh` home car

ries that file; browser localStorage is outside `.dsh` and does not;
- the browser merges those fold
ers into the Workspace list it derives from (`mergePluginFolders` in src/client/tree.ts) and attribu
tes Sessions to a Workspace by matching their `cwd` against the list — the host leaves such Sessions

ungrouped, so only unclaimed ones are borrowed;
- adding and removing folders works from the projec
t editor exactly as it does on a newer host. Clicking a folder's own name opens that folder in the O
S file manager — the *Set as primary* and remove buttons inside the row keep their own actions; a fo
lder that has since disappeared says so inline in the dialog instead of only logging it.
The node half also tells the model about them. It registers a prompt context (`workspace-browser:fol
ders`, order `SANDBOX_POLICY + 1`) that resolves the Session's Workspace from `ctx.workspaceRegistry
` — membership first, then an exact `cwd` match, then the deepest folder containing the `cwd`, which
is what finds a Session started in a promoted folder — and renders:

That sentence is the whole mechanism: the host's `workspace-write` policy still resolves a single ro
ot (`session.header.cwd`), so the plugin can widen what the model *knows*, never what it may *write*
. Under `danger-full-access` the write caveat is moot. Nothing is injected when the Workspace has no
extra folder, when the Session is unknown to the registry, or when the host has no `systemPrompt` s
folder, when the Session is unknown to the registry, or when the host has no `systemPrompt` service.

## Install

The GUI plugin manager does the same. `cordis.patch.yml` is declared by `dsh.bundle.patch`, so it mu
st stay in `files`: a packed package (git or npm install) that lacks it is rejected with `failed to
les`: a packed package (git or npm install) that lacks it is rejected with `failed to read overlay`.
The host composes plugin node halves at startup, so a change to `lib/index.js` shows up only after t
he app restarts — including the prompt context below, whose text is resolved at every Session prompt
assembly. The client half is unaffected by that restart rule.
## Build
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`scripts/bundle-node.mjs` is the fallback for the node half when no harness checkout is available: i
t concatenates `lib/types` into the single-file `lib/index.js` the package entry names, which is exa
ctly the transformation the preset's Node build face performs for these three modules. The client ha
lf still needs the preset.
`scripts/build-client.mjs` uses the client-bundle preset from a dsh source checkout (`packages/clien
t/tsdown.client.ts`, default `..\..\deepseek-harness`, override with `$DSH_HARNESS` or an argument).
The preset resolves a package through `packages/<group>/<dir>/package.json`, so the script stages a
temporary face package inside the checkout, links this repo's `node_modules` into it, runs tsdown f
or the Client face, normalizes the checkout path out of the emitted banners, copies the artifacts ba
ck and deletes the staging directory. The checkout itself is left untouched.
